title: The Weather App (Chas McIvor)
style: jazz lounge piano bar dry wit spoken word observational 104bpm upright bass brushed snare deadpan baritone male vocal life philosophy absurdist technology Perth Zimbabwe
lyrics:
[Verse 1]
The weather app says forty percent chance of rain at three
And I make decisions based on that particular certainty
That isn't quite certainty — it's an assessment of the possible
Which I've translated into definitely — that's the plausible

[Pre-Chorus]
The weather app has been wrong on my specific street before
And I've had that conversation with the app — it doesn't respond to more

[Chorus]
The weather app knows something I don't know
It knows the models and the satellites and the wind's preferred flow
The weather app has seventeen data inputs from around the sky
And still can't tell me if I need an umbrella — and that's why
That's my boy

[Verse 2]
There are five different weather apps and they all say different things
And the truth is somewhere in the range of what each one brings
To the table — and the table is my phone and the phone
Shows me five conflicting futures that I'll have to face alone

[Bridge]
In Zimbabwe the weather was read from the sky and from the behaviour
Of the animals and birds who had no need of a data saviour
And they were right more often than the apps
Although I acknowledge this comparison has some gaps

[Outro]
Weather app knows… and doesn't know… and knows again…
That's my boy
